core.title: Derive artifact cardinality from the aspect's plurality
core.given: An artifact name of colon-separated segments ending in an aspect (the final noun), optionally preceded by category segments (categories are not required) and optionally followed by a variant.
core.when: The artifact's cardinality (one item vs collection) is determined or interpreted, whether for a new name or an existing one.
core.then: Take cardinality from the ASPECT (the final noun before any variant) alone: plural aspect → collection/array schema or directory of items; singular aspect → single-item schema.
prefer: Identify the aspect first (the final noun before the variant), then read its plurality to pick or interpret the shape.
Pluralize the aspect when you mean a collection; keep it singular for one item.
avoid: Inferring cardinality from a category segment: a plural category does not make the artifact a collection (a name with plural category segments and a singular aspect is still one item).
Letting the variant segment change cardinality.
Declaring an array/directory under a singular aspect, or a single-item schema under a plural aspect.
core.why: Cardinality (single item vs collection) is decided by the aspect's plurality, so the name alone indicates one item or a collection; categories and variants do not affect cardinality.
evidence: For each artifact name, the reviewer identifies the aspect and confirms plural aspect ↔ collection/array schema or directory of items, singular aspect ↔ single-item schema.
Reviewer confirms category and variant segments were not used to decide cardinality.
verification: Scope: any determination or interpretation of an artifact's cardinality — for new or existing names — with no phase or document-type restriction.

Per artifact name, the check identifies the aspect (the final noun before any variant; names need not contain a category segment) and confirms the mapping: singular aspect = single-item schema; plural aspect = collection/array schema or directory of items; category position and variant position do not affect cardinality.

Activating on changes requires an observer that extracts artifact names (segmented, with or without category segments) and any associated shape from new or existing text; absent such an observer, activation relies on task terms.
An aspect-plurality disagreement with the declared cardinality is an optional detection signal, not an activation prerequisite: the rule also applies when interpreting conforming names.
Identifying the aspect vs category/variant segments and its plurality requires judgment unless the realization supplies a parser and a plural lexicon.

values: artifact name declared, changed or referenced
artifact shape (single item vs collection/array/directory) declared or read
aspect plurality disagrees with declared cardinality

fires: An artifact name is declared whose aspect is plural and its shape must be set.
An existing artifact name with a singular aspect is read and its cardinality must be interpreted.
An artifact name has a plural category segment and its cardinality must be determined or interpreted.
A name with no category segment whose cardinality is in question.
A conforming name and shape are being checked or relied on, even when no mismatch exists.
doesNotFire: Text that neither declares, references nor interprets any artifact name or artifact cardinality.
Choosing the physical file/directory layout itself (covered by the logical-physical mapping convention), once cardinality is already settled.
Spelling of plurals (covered by the pluralization convention).

neutralityNotes: This rule is a semantic artifact-naming convention with no stack mechanism, so the core is essentially the Bun text minus its concrete example names (scenario:*, commons:ux:*), which remain in bun.json as the delivered reference example (see bunOnly). The colon-separated segment scheme is the subject matter of this rule family (naming-pattern, pluralization, logical-physical mapping) rather than a stack mechanism, so it stays in the core's given without a profile key; it names no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, suffix or path, and 'array'/'directory' are used only as generic shape words. Activation is deliberately unscoped to any document type, phase, root or file kind (per the source's own note), so the core needs no profile values and profileRequirements/proposedKeys are empty. The activation facts' explanatory notes have no place in the core fact shape and are preserved as verifier scope in core.verification.
